subject: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs Orchid Labs
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Mike Larson <mike@orchidlabs.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs Orchid Labs

Hi Mike — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Key pain points you shared
- Latency spikes at 95th/99th percentile on peak patient messaging windows (~200–300 concurrent sessions).
- Cost per active user is a blocker for scaling triage workflows to more clinics.
- Need for VPC/private deployment and strict audit logging for HIPAA compliance.

Goals for the bake-off
1) Match current throughput while lowering per-token cost by >=25%.
2) 95th percentile response time <= 300ms for standard triage prompts.
3) Validate private deployment (VPC) and logging proof points for 3rd-party audit.

Decision criteria (what Orchid will score)
- Latency (p95/p99) on standard prompt set
- Token cost and predictable unit economics at scale
- VPC/on-prem support and KMS integration
- Output quality on clinical prompts (ROUGE/QA pass rate)
- Support & SLA (SLOs, incident response)

Open questions we flagged
- Which model sizes are you planning to include in the test (we should align model families).
- Is there a subset of live patient examples you can provide as anonymized test prompts?

What Redwood will deliver
- Perf test plan and synthetic load harness (attached: perf_test_plan.pdf).
- Short comparison spreadsheet summarizing Redwood vs two competitors (attached: redwood_vs_competitor_summary.xlsx).
- SOC2 snapshot and security notes (attached: SOC2_snapshot.zip).

Proposed immediate next steps
- Share anonymized test prompt subset from Orchid (owner: Mike) — by EOW (Nov 10).
- Redwood to run initial perf baseline against your sample prompts on Tuesday (Nov 10–11) and share results by Nov 12 (owner: Aisha).
- Schedule a live results review + Q&A on Friday Nov 13, 10:00–11:00 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite.
- Procurement: connect procurement@orchidlabs.com with our sales ops to scope PO terms if bake-off looks good (owner: Mike / procurement).

If that all looks right, I’ll kick off the perf harness and share the Drive link to test artifacts.

Thanks — talk soon.

Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference
From: Mike Larson <mike@orchidlabs.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orchidlabs.com
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs Orchid Labs

Thanks Aisha — nice summary. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) We can share a de-identified sample of about 1,200 prompts. I’ll get legal to sign the NDA scoping addendum and send the files by Monday morning.
2) For models, the internal team is most interested in small/medium quantized variants (to evaluate cost) plus one fp16 large model to validate quality. Can Redwood run both quantized + fp16 for the same prompt set?
3) Procurement: we target a decision by the end of November. We’d like the bake-off results and one week of follow-up to present to the leadership committee.

Also, can you confirm whether the perf test will simulate our traffic pattern (bursty with 90-minute peaks) vs constant QPS? Prefer realistic burst profiles if possible.

—Mike
Director of Engineering, Orchid Labs
mike@orchidlabs.com | (650) 555-0199

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs Orchid Labs

Thanks Mike — all good notes. Short answers:
- Yes, we can run both quantized (INT8/4) and fp16 variants in parallel and include side-by-side cost/latency tables. Aditya will own the quantization matrix and configurations.
- We will simulate your bursty traffic profile (90–120 minute peaks) in the perf harness; plan runs will include both realistic burst windows and steady-state tests.
- Timeline looks fine for a late-Nov decision; we’ll prioritize the initial baseline and aim to have results back by Nov 12.

What I’m sending now:
- Drive link with perf test plan and test harness (https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2B3C4D-test-plan)
- Initial checklist for anonymized prompt ingest (attached in the Drive).

Next actions (owners/dates)
- Mike: Share anonymized prompt set + any special edge-case prompts by Mon Nov 9 (we’ll accept secure upload to the Drive).
- Aditya: Run quantized + fp16 baseline runs Nov 10–11 (owner: aditya_rao).
- Rishi: I copied security for a quick SOC2 Q&A if Orchid wants anything specific before the test (owner: rishi_malhotra).
- Aisha: Send calendar invite for results review (Nov 13, 10:00–11:00 PT).

I’ll also attach the spreadsheet with the initial vendor comparison and a short perf test plan (see attachments). If anything changes on your side, ping me and we’ll adjust.

Invite to follow.

Best,
Aisha

Attachments: redwood_vs_competitor_summary.xlsx, perf_test_plan.pdf, SOC2_snapshot.zip
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 15:32:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs Orchid Labs (internal)

Internal note — looping you two on the bake-off. Key asks:
- Aditya: prioritize quantized config matrix and a short doc describing how we’ll measure cost (tokens + infra). Goal: have baseline runs Nov 10–11.
- Marissa: attach a one-pager on pricing options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) tailored to Orchid’s scale; procurement will want an apples-to-apples.
- Rishi: please review the SOC2 snapshot I attached and flag anything Orchid might ask for proactively.

We’ll treat this as a high-probability mid-market deal with a late-Nov decision window — keep CS on standby in case we need a deeper quality pass.

Thanks — Aisha
